source.title: Where First-Order and Monadic Second-Order Logic Coincide

accepted.question_text: Which graph classes C that are closed under taking induced subgraphs have the property that first-order logic and monadic second-order logic define the same graph properties when formulas are interpreted only on graphs in C?
accepted.context_brief: FO versus MSO on induced-subgraph-closed graph classes

evidence.quote: Indeed, it is an open problem for which classes C of graphs closed under taking induced subgraphs FO ≡C MSO holds.

accepted.question_text: For variants of monadic second-order logic such as MSO with parity predicates, which test whether quantified relations have even cardinality, what kind of first-order logic is needed to combine the logical types of an unbounded number of substructures, and for which such monadic second-order logics can those type-combination methods be developed?
accepted.context_brief: Composition theorems for MSO variants with parity

evidence.quote: Another direction is to consider other kinds of monadic second-order logics like MSO with parity predicates, which test whether bound relations have even cardinality.
Which kind of first-order logics do we need to combine the types of which kinds of monadic second-order logics?
